questions.question: Which of the following is called 'the safety valve of nature'?
questions.solution:
• **Volcanoes** are known as the safety valves of nature
 
• A safety valve is an opening that opens up to release built-up pressure inside equipment which can cause the equipment to dysfunction 
 
• Similarly, there are huge pressures and high temperatures inside the Earth as you go closer to the Earth's core
 
• This pressure is sometimes relieved in the form of volcanic eruptions that discharge large amounts of magma, heat and gases that are built up within the Earth and thus it is known as 'a safety valve' of the planet

questions.question: Build-up of which acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps?
questions.solution:
• Whenever sudden activity of a muscle takes place the muscles cannot be supplied with enough oxygen.
 
• To satisfy the need of energy anaerobic respiration takes place forming lactic acid as the by product. Lactic acid causes pain and stiffness in the muscles.

questions.question: A bullet of mass 10 g is ﬁred with a velocity of 20 m/s from a gun of mass 2 kg. Find the recoil velocity (in m/s) of the gun.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The mass of the ejected body and the mass of the recoiling body are related to one another by the law of conservation of momentum which is obtained from **Newton’s laws of motion**.
 
• According to the **law of conservation of momentum**, for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Recoiling velocity is an example of this law. From the law, it can be said that
 
 
• **m₁ v₁ = - m₂ v₂**
 
• m1 and v1 are the mass and velocity of the bullet
 
• m2 and v2 are the mass and velocity of the gun
 
 

 
• Here m₁= 10g = 0.01 kg, v₁ = 20 m/s and m₂ = 2 kg, 

⇒ m₁ v₁ = - m₂ v₂

⇒ 0.01 x 20 = - 2 x v₂

⇒ v₂ = 0.2 / 2 =** 0.1 m/s**

**Note: **Recoil velocity will always be **negative **as the gun will always move in the opposite direction of the fired bullet.

questions.question: The product of force and the time for which the force acts on a body is equal to the change in ________ of the body.
questions.solution:
• The statement is from Newton’s Second Law of Motion which states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the resultant force applied and is in the direction of the resultant force.
 
• The resultant force is equal to the rate of change of momentum.

questions.question: Earthquake tremors are caused by the disturbance deep down inside the uppermost layer of the earth called the ________.
questions.solution:
• Most earthquakes occur along the edge of the oceanic and continental plates. The earth's crust (the outer layer of the planet) is made up of several pieces called plates.
 
• The plates under the oceans are called oceanic plates and the rest are continental plates. Earthquakes usually occur where two plates are running into each other or sliding past each other.
